previous_statement: With Y=(Y_i) and V=(V_i), rectangular matrix multiplication gives Y^dagger dot V = sum_i Y_i^dagger dot V_i. Node 1.3.1 gives Y_i^dagger dot V_i=<Y_i,V_i>*u_Q for each i. Therefore Y^dagger dot V=sum_i(<Y_i,V_i>*u_Q)=(sum_i<Y_i,V_i>)*u_Q=<Y,V>_n*u_Q, where the penultimate equality is finite distributivity of scalar multiplication and the last is exactly the defining coordinate formula in the preceding child. Suppressing the amplification subscript yields the assertion of nodes 1.3.2 and 1.3.
new_statement: With Y=(Y_i) and V=(V_i), rectangular matrix multiplication and the coordinate identities of node 1.3.1 yield only Y^dagger dot V=sum_i(Y_i^dagger dot V_i)=sum_i(<Y_i,V_i>*u_Q)=(sum_i<Y_i,V_i>)*u_Q. The presently allowed definitions do not identify sum_i<Y_i,V_i> with the separately named amplified form <Y,V>_n: replacing that level-n form by 2*sum_i<Y_i,V_i> preserves every registered input but changes the claimed equality. Hence the former assertion <Y,V>_n*u_Q, and therefore the claimed deduction of nodes 1.3.2 and 1.3 from this step, is not justified unless the canonical coordinate-sum normalization of the amplified form is added as an allowed definition or validated dependency.
